notYet: Not yet part of the Western Mediterranean

stages.name: Native peoples
stages.desc: Nuragic, Libyan, Iberian and other local societies, under no outside power

stages.name: Phoenician ally
stages.desc: Independent Phoenician towns, increasingly in Carthage's orbit

stages.name: Greek
stages.desc: Dominated by Greek cities and settlers

states.name: France
timeline: Greek Massalia leads the south coast and Alalia stands on Corsica; Celtic peoples inland

states.name: Spain
timeline: Iberian peoples inland; Phoenician Gadir and its sister towns on the south coast

states.name: Libya
timeline: Phoenician towns such as Lepcis on the west coast; Greek Cyrene in the east
Carthaginians and Libyans drive the Spartan Dorieus from Cinyps

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage and its nearby coast; inland, the Libyans still collect rent for the city's ground
Malchus's exiled army besieges and takes Carthage, by Justin's account
Himera is lost, but the city keeps its territory and pays an indemnity

states.name: Italy
timeline: Etruscan cities lead the centre; Greeks hold the south and east of Sicily; Phoenicians and Nuragic peoples share Sardinia
Malchus's army is destroyed in Sardinia
Hamilcar holds south-west Sardinia for Carthage; the mountains stay Nuragic
Rome's treaty with Carthage recognises a Carthaginian part of Sicily
Gelon and Theron crush Hamilcar's army at Himera in Sicily

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Libyan peoples, with small Phoenician harbours along the coast

states.name: Malta
timeline: Phoenician settlers on the sea lane between Sicily and Africa
The islands pass into Carthage's orbit; the date is approximate

events.title: Tyre's western daughter
events.text: Carthage, founded from Tyre by tradition in 814 BC, still sends a yearly tithe to Melqart in its mother city.

events.title: Rent to the Libyans
events.text: Justin says Carthage owes the Libyans a regular payment for the ground the city stands on.

events.title: Libyan country
events.text: Inland North Africa belongs to Libyan peoples, with only small Phoenician harbours on the coast.

events.title: Phoenician Sardinia
events.text: Sulci and its sister towns have traded and lived alongside Nuragic Sardinians for some three centuries.

events.title: Nuragic Sardinia
events.text: Communities such as S'Urachi live around great stone towers built centuries earlier.

events.title: Phoenician Motya
events.text: An island town off western Sicily anchors the Phoenician corner of the island.

events.title: Greek Massalia
events.text: Phocaean Greeks, settled here since about 600 BC, trade up the Rhône.

events.title: Phoenician Gadir
events.text: The old Tyrian town beyond the Strait of Gibraltar grows rich on Atlantic trade and Iberian metals.

events.title: Etruscan Caere
events.text: One of the great Etruscan sea powers, soon to be Carthage's partner.

events.title: Malchus in Sicily
events.text: Justin says the general Malchus conquers part of Sicily; he gives no date, and this one is an estimate.

events.title: Phocaean refugees
events.text: Fleeing the Persian conquest of Ionia, more Phocaeans settle at Alalia, and Herodotus says they raid their neighbours.

events.title: Defeat in Sardinia
events.text: Justin says Malchus loses the greater part of his army in a great battle; the site is unknown.

events.title: Malchus exiled
events.text: Carthage sentences the general and his surviving soldiers to exile.

events.title: Exiles besiege Carthage
events.text: Their pleas refused, Malchus's soldiers cross to Africa and blockade their own city.

events.title: Carthalo crucified
events.text: Malchus has his son, a priest back from Tyre, nailed to a high cross in view of the walls.

events.title: Carthage falls
events.text: Malchus takes the city, pardons most opponents and executes ten senators.

events.title: Malchus executed
events.text: Accused of seeking kingship, Malchus is put to death, by Justin's account.

events.title: Battle of Alalia
events.text: Sixty Greek ships beat a Carthaginian and Etruscan fleet twice their size, but lose forty ships and abandon Corsica.

events.title: Prisoners stoned
events.text: Herodotus says the men of Caere stone their Greek captives to death.

events.title: Mago takes command
events.text: Justin says Mago succeeds Malchus and is first to build Carthage's power through military discipline.

events.title: Fire at Monte Sirai
events.text: Burnt layers here were long read as Carthaginian conquest; recent work stresses continuity instead.

events.title: Elea founded
events.text: Phocaean survivors of Alalia settle on the Italian coast at Elea, after a first refuge at Rhegion.

events.title: Battle of Cumae
events.text: Greek Cumae beats back an Etruscan attack, by the traditional date.

events.title: Mago's sons
events.text: Hasdrubal and Hamilcar inherit their father's command, founding a dynasty of generals.

events.title: War for Sardinia
events.text: The brothers carry the war back to the island where Malchus lost his army.

events.title: War over the rent
events.text: The Libyans fight Carthage for years of unpaid rent; Justin says it ends with Carthage paying.

events.title: Dorieus at Cinyps
events.text: The Spartan prince Dorieus founds a colony on Libya's coast, inside Carthage's sphere.

events.title: Dorieus expelled
events.text: In the third year, Carthaginians and Libyans drive the Spartans out.

events.title: Hasdrubal dies
events.text: Wounded in Sardinia, the holder of eleven dictatorships and four triumphs dies, and Hamilcar takes command.

events.title: Dorieus killed
events.text: Dorieus tries again near Eryx in western Sicily, and dies there with most of his men.

events.title: Sybaris destroyed
events.text: Croton wipes out its wealthy Greek neighbour, showing how divided the western Greeks are.

events.title: Treaty with Rome
events.text: Polybius preserves a treaty limiting Roman trade in Sardinia and Libya; its early date is debated.

events.title: Pani Loriga
events.text: Excavation dates the Punic phase of this inland Sardinian stronghold to around 500 BC.

events.title: Pyrgi tablets
events.text: Gold tablets in Etruscan and Phoenician record a temple to Astarte built by Thefarie Velianas of Caere.

events.title: Punic Ibiza
events.text: Ibiza grows into a Punic town on the sea road to Iberia.

events.title: Terillus expelled
events.text: Theron of Acragas drives Terillus from Himera, and Terillus asks his friend Hamilcar for help.

events.title: Hostages from Rhegion
events.text: Anaxilas of Rhegion backs his father-in-law by sending his own children to Hamilcar as hostages.

events.title: Hamilcar's army
events.text: Herodotus lists Phoenicians, Libyans, Iberians, Ligurians, Elisyci, Sardinians and Corsicans; his 300,000 is far too high.

events.title: Iberian soldiers
events.text: Herodotus names Iberians among the peoples who march in Hamilcar's army.

events.title: Elisyci recruited
events.text: Men from around Narbonne march in Hamilcar's army, showing how far Carthage now recruits.

events.title: Battle of Himera
events.text: Gelon of Syracuse and Theron of Acragas destroy the Carthaginian army and burn its ships.

events.title: Hamilcar vanishes
events.text: Diodorus says disguised horsemen killed him; Carthaginians told Herodotus he threw himself into the sacrificial fire.

events.title: The price of defeat
events.text: Carthage pays Syracuse two thousand talents of silver, but loses no territory.

events.title: Salamis
events.text: Herodotus places Himera on the same day as the Greek naval victory here, a coincidence historians doubt.

chartNote: Share of the land shown, by the power that dominated each region; today's boundaries, a deliberate simplification. Most regions held several peoples at once, and large desert regions swing the shares. Dates before about 510 BC are estimates, because Justin gives none, and whether Malchus existed is debated.
